title: Projectivity of the compactified ball modification when a Kato manifold has Kähler universal cover
author: Nicolina Istrati; Alexandra Otiman; Massimiliano Pontecorvo; Matteo Ruggiero
difficulty_reason: Miyaoka extension and Moishezon projectivity do not transfer the universal-cover Kahler form to the modified ball on their own. Proposition2.4 constructs compatible holomorphic embeddings by iterating the Kato fundamental domains and proving that they exhaust the punctured modified ball. Lemma10.2 then glues the pulled-back form to a Fubini–Study multiple through a controlled regularized maximum, providing the new construction needed before the final projectivity theorem applies.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem10.3 implication(2)⇒(3) only, for a Kato datum consisting of a proper modification at the origin of the complex n-ball and a holomorphic embedded sub-ball, with associated Kato manifold and the induced compactification modification of CP^n. Kähler universal cover implies that compactified modification is projective. Full new iterated-domain embedding Proposition2.4 physical7–8, Kähler collar regularized-maximum construction Lemma10.2 physical44, and implication proof45 read. Miyaoka removable-point extension, local dd^c potential for the pushed positive closed form, regularized maximum and Kähler–Moishezon theorem are explicit established foundations; the new gluing/open-embedding construction remains authored core. Lemma10.2 prints pluriharmonic while explicitly using a strictly plurisubharmonic potential dd^c psi for a positive form; preserve that literal typo and the surrounding strict-psh/regularized-maximum formulas. No new potential supplied. General equivalence(4)⇒(1) refers to an earlier smooth-blowup theorem then says same proof works for arbitrary Kähler modifications without writing that extension, so that direction and full equivalence are excluded. No toric-specific/Hodge/metric nonexistence corollary counted.
